author: AI Editorial Team (Esi)
key_learning_objective: Select appropriate low-sodium food choices for a client with heart failure.
question_stem: A nurse is teaching a client with heart failure about a low-sodium diet. Which food choices indicate the client understands the teaching? Select all that apply.

rationales.A: Correct. Fresh, unprocessed meats are naturally low in sodium.
rationales.B: Canned soups are typically very high in sodium.
rationales.C: Correct. Fresh vegetables without added salt are low-sodium choices.
rationales.D: Processed/deli meats are high in sodium preservatives.
rationales.E: Correct. Fresh fruit is naturally low in sodium.
rationales.F: Pickled and brined foods are high in sodium.

key_takeaway: Fresh = low sodium; canned, processed, cured, and pickled = high sodium.
nclex_test_taking_tip: For low-sodium diets, 'fresh and unprocessed' is almost always the safe pick.
memory_trick: If it comes in a can or a package, assume it's salty.
clinical_pearls: Typical HF target is ~2 g sodium/day.
Teach label reading: sodium per serving and servings per container.
